control_flow: driveInTheDark: if RLIGHT is above 75 %, drive forward at 30 %; else call stopAtWall.
stopAtWall: if an obstacle is ahead, stop; else call followLine.
followLine: if the line tracker sees black, curve left; else curve right.

likely_intent.description: Follow the black line, drive straight through a dark tunnel without touching its walls, and follow the line again after the tunnel.

decision_points.condition: the right light sensor reads above 75 %

branches.outcome: bright light: it drives forward at 30 %
an obstacle is ahead: it stops

scenarios.coded_response: In bright light it drives straight at 30 %; in the dark with no line it curves right; after the tunnel it drives straight again.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot starts on a black line in bright light; the line runs into a dark tunnel with no line inside and continues after it.
scenarios.trigger: It follows the line into the tunnel and out again.

assumptions: The line continues after the tunnel.
The dark tunnel has no line inside.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It follows the line, drives straight through the dark tunnel without touching its walls, and follows the line again after the tunnel.

scenarios.coded_response: It stops while the obstacle is ahead.

assumptions: 'Without touching its walls' includes a wall ahead.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It stops before the wall without touching it.

scenarios.coded_response: It follows the line in the dark: curves left on black and right on the floor.

uncertainties: The program drives straight in bright light, so it does not follow the line there.
In a dark tunnel with no line it curves right, not straight.
It stops at an obstacle ahead in the dark, so a wall blocks it instead of driving through.
After the tunnel, bright light makes it drive straight again, not follow the line.
Following the line again after the tunnel can't be tested reliably: a right line follower may lose the line in the dark.
